Order 
 IN  S.B. CRIMINAL REVISION PETITION NO.531/1996  (Riyasat Ali Khan @ Bundu Khan Vs. State of Rajasthan)
Date of Order : 02.08.2016  HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE GOVERDHAN BARDHAR Mr. Chandraveer Singh, for the petitioner.

sentences.text: Mr. L.R. Upadhyay, Public Prosecutor.
BY THE COURT

The petitioner by way of present revision petition under Section 397/401 Cr.P.C. has assailed the impugned judgment dated 10.12.1996 passed by learned Additional Sessions Judge, Nagaur Camp Deedwana (hereinafter "the Appellate Court") in Criminal Appeal No.7/1994 whereby the learned appellate Court has upheld the judgment dated 16.02.1994, passed by the Civil Judge and Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate, Deedwana (for short "the trial court") in Cr. Case No.666/1992 whereby the trial court convicted the accused-petitioner for offence under Section 16(1)(a)(ii) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 (for short, 'PFA Act') read with Rule 50 of the PFA Rules and sentenced him to undergo one year's rigorous imprisonment alongwith fine of Rs. 1000/- and in default thereof to undergone two months' simple imprisonment.

entities.text: Additional Sessions Judge, Nagaur Camp Deedwana
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Brief facts, giving rise to this revision petition are that on 18.07.1986, the Food Inspector inspected the shop of Bodu Khan situated at Bus Stand Beri Khurd and found that he was selling the food products without having the food licence.

On the complaint, cognizance under Section 16/50 of PFA Act was S.B. CRIMINAL REVISION PETITION NO.531/1996 (Riyasat Ali Khan @ Bundu Khan Vs.
State of Rajasthan) taken against the accused Bodu Khan and he was summoned.

entities.text:
S.B. CRIMINAL REVISION PETITION NO.531/1996 (Riyasat Ali Khan @ Bundu Khan Vs.
State of Rajasthan)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The accused Bodu Khan filed an application on 14.02.1992 stating that his name is Riyasat Ali and not Bodu Khan.

Investigation in this regard was carried out and the trial court on 13/09/1993 reached on the conclusion that Bodu Khan and Riyasat Ali was one and the same person and rejected the petitioner's application.
Thereafter, before framing of charge, statement of Mahipal Sharma (PW-1) was recorded.
The learned trial Court framed charge against the petitioner for offence punishable under Section 16/50 of PFA Act.
The accused denied the charge and claimed for trial.

After conclusion of the prosecution evidence, statement of the accused under Section 313 Cr.P.C.
was recorded.

The learned trial Court, thereafter, heard final arguments and by its judgment dated Riyasat Wali Khan vs State on 2 August, 2016 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/187153858/
1 16.02.1994, convicted the accused-petitioner for offence under Section 16(1)(a)(ii) of PFA Act read with Rule 50 of PFA Rules and passed the sentence of one year's rigorous imprisonment with fine of Rs.1000/-.

entities.text: Riyasat Wali Khan vs State on 2 August, 2016 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In default of payment of fine, the trial court ordered that the petitioner shall undergo two months' simple imprisonment.
Being aggrieved by the judgment of the learned trial Court, the accused-petitioner approached the learned appellate Court.
The appellate Court by its judgment dated 10.12.1996 dismissed the petitioner's appeal and upheld the conviction and sentence awarded by the trial court.

At the outset, learned counsel for the petitioner submits S.B. CRIMINAL REVISION PETITION NO.531/1996 (Riyasat Ali Khan @ Bundu Khan Vs. State of Rajasthan) that he is not challenging the conviction of the petitioner for offence Section 16(1)(a)(ii) of PFA Act read with Rule 50 of PFA Rules recorded by the learned trial court and affirmed by the learned appellate court but his only prayer is for issuance of direction to the State Government to consider case of the petitioner for commutation of sentence.

entities.text: S.B. CRIMINAL REVISION PETITION NO.531/1996 (Riyasat Ali Khan @ Bundu Khan Vs. State of Rajasthan
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the petitioner further submits that the petitioner is not a habitual offender and therefore, his case for commutation of sentence can very well be considered by the Government under Section 433(d) Cr.P.C.

In support of this plea, learned counsel has placed reliance on decision of Hon'ble Supreme Court and High Court in the case of N.Sukumaran Nair V/s. Food 4 Inspector, Mavelikara [1995 SC CANDID 80] and Deva V/s. State of Rajasthan [2015 2 RLW(Raj.) 1002; 2014 Supreme(Raj) 544].

entities.text: N.Sukumaran Nair V/s. Food 4 Inspector, Mavelikara [1995 SC CANDID 80]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: Deva V/s. State of Rajasthan [2015 2 RLW(Raj.) 1002; 2014 Supreme(Raj) 544]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Learned Public Prosecutor has not opposed the prayer in general and submitted that in some of the identical cases, directions have been issued by the Court for consideration of commutation of sentence.
I have heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the materials available on record.

It is not disputed that the petitioner is not a habitual offender and therefore, the prayer to examine the case of the petitioner for commutation of sentence is acceptable.
In N.Sukumaran (supra), Supreme Court examined the matter on the touchstone of Section 433(d)
Cr.P.C. and held :
"3. The offence took place in the year 1984.

The appellant has been awarded six months' simple imprisonment and has also been ordered to pay a fine of Rs.1,000.00 Under S.B. CRIMINAL REVISION PETITION NO.531/1996 (Riyasat Ali Khan @
Bundu Khan Vs. State of Rajasthan) clause (d) of Section 433 of the Code of Criminal Procedure

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: , "the appropriate government" is empowered to commute the sentence of simple imprisonment for fine.
We think that this would be an appropriate case for commutation of sentence where almost a decade has gone by.

We, therefore, direct the appellant to deposit in the trial court a sum of Rs.6,000.00 as fine in commutation of the sentence of six months' simple imprisonment within a 5 period of six weeks form today and intimate to the appropriate government that such fine has been deposited.

On deposit of such fine, the State Government may formalise the Riyasat Wali Khan vs State on 2 August, 2016 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/187153858/
2 matter by passing appropriate orders under clause (d) of Section 433 of the Code of Criminal Procedures."

entities.text: Riyasat Wali Khan vs State on 2 August, 2016 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: A co-ordinate Bench of this Court in Deva(supra) following the verdict in N.Sukumaran (supra) and taking into account the fact that incident is too old, held as under :
"9. The offence took place in the year 1981.
The accused petitioner has been awarded the imprisonment as indicated above.
Under Clause (d) of Section 433 of the Cr.P.C.
The appropriate government is empowered to commute the sentence of simple imprisonment for fine.
10. I think that this would be an appropriate case for commutation of sentence where almost a decade has gone by.

I, therefore, direct the petitioner to deposit in the trial Court a sum of Rs.6,000/- as fine in commutation of the sentence of six months simple imprisonment within a period of six weeks from today and intimate to the appropriate government that such fine has been deposited.

On deposit of such fine, the State Government may formalise the matter by passing appropriate orders; under Clause (d) of Section 433 of Cr.P.C. Till then the petitioner will remain on same bail bonds."
Undisputedly, since conviction of the petitioner, there is nothing adverse against him so as to prove that he is involved in food adulteration.

In this view of the matter and considering the S.B.
CRIMINAL REVISION PETITION NO.531/1996 (Riyasat Ali Khan @ Bundu Khan Vs. State of Rajasthan) fact that the incident has occurred about 30 years back, I deem it just and appropriate to direct the petitioner to deposit a sum of Rs.7,500/- as fine before learned trial Court in commutation of sentence of one year's rigorous imprisonment for offence under Section 16(1)(a)(ii) of PFA Act read with Rule 50 of PFA Rules within a period of two months from today.

S.B.
CRIMINAL REVISION PETITION NO.531/1996 (Riyasat Ali Khan @ Bundu Khan Vs. State of Rajasthan)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
After deposition of the aforesaid amount, the petitioner may intimate the appropriate Government so as to formalize the matter by passing appropriate orders; under Clause (d) of Section 433 Cr.P.C. Till then the matter is formalized by the State Government for passing appropriate orders for commutation of sentence,
the petitioner shall remain on the same bail bonds.
With these observations, the revision petition is disposed of.

(GOVERDHAN BARDHAR),J.
